admission.justification: The converted-memory journey test distinguishes the pre-revision refusal from the post-adoption not-recorded state and checks their next actions even after cards and a baseline exist; these artifacts do not establish an authored foundation.

applicability: The knowledge block of memory_init results in the converted-memory initialization and first-baseline journey, before the first memory revision and after adoption when no knowledge foundation has been authored.
conditions: Before the first memory revision, the knowledge block reports context-not-admitted with code memory_revision_unavailable and a nonempty nextAction.

After baseline adoption with cards present but no authored knowledge foundation, the knowledge block reports not-recorded and nextAction directs the developer to start the Architect, not knowledge-bootstrap.
exclusions: Declaring foundation completion because cards or a baseline exist.
Changing product state to match an inaccurate example in prose.
The retired c-03-repo-bootstrap hand-off procedure, its card inventory and clean fixer dry-run obligations.

evidence: journey read-back (cards, sidecars bcc0d9df commit, text/v2 read) + composed journey test proving both knowledge moments (context-not-admitted/memory_revision_unavailable pre-baseline, not-recorded post-baseline); architect ruling rule 5(a) notes/run3/L45-THE-HAND-OFF-NAMES-THE-STATE-MEMORY-INIT-REPORTS-AT-THAT-MOMENT-RULING.json

statement: memory_init reports the knowledge state at the observed memory revision with its named next step; cards or an attributed baseline do not by themselves establish an authored knowledge foundation.
